title: CI scope skips every job on a push that changes only docs/records.md when the head before the push was fully green
why:
Owner ruling own-830-c-ci-scope-green-before-head (page item 830, option c, 15:02 CST Nov 14, no note); the owner chose a widening knowingly. Today a ready green PR meets a records-page push at merge (about 4 of 11 PR-merge commits since Nov 13 and 20 of 38 since Nov 10, triage's approximate count from a shallow clone) and a second full CI follows (44 min 32 s in the one run measured, n=1: run 43583006785, #3349 head 3128df369). The change, as the records lane described it (relayed, unread by triage): ci-scope.sh reads the push's before-head, checks that head's run was fully green and the push changed docs/records.md alone, then sets every job flag false; all-jobs-passed counts those skipped jobs as passed. It changes ci-scope.sh, checks.yml and lint/test_ci_scope.py, and edits the script's own fail-safe list, so it needs review round 3 and the net-value test. Unmeasured: the gain (jobs flagged false still start and skip), and a fail-safe against a wrong green read. GRANT SCOPE: only a push whose whole change is docs/records.md after a fully green head; any other change in the push runs CI as today. First act of a lane: read ci-scope.sh line 17 on (it diffs the whole PR against its base, never the push) and the test file, write the red tests first: a records-only push after a green head skips; a records-only push after a red or unknown head runs; a push that touches one other file runs; a hand-edited page does not skip beyond what main's check allows. Triage reads the before-head result as unknown when the run cannot be read, never as green. Kin: records-page-before-ready (the lane that described it), ready-push-merges-main (item 840), review-carries-own-record-commits. LANE 15:11 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 15:09, its pick, told the lane 15:08): the records lane session_013NEJKzSUfg1GuTrqARWDNd builds it on a new branch; it also tells the coordinator whether #3396 is moot. MECHANISM CHANGED 15:14 CST Nov 14 (the records lane, accepted by the coordinator 15:12 as its own undoable pick; triage read none): the lane changed the mechanism from the step text (the push's before-head) to a green-head reader, because the ready route has no push before-head (the draft run skips scope). The delta is measured from the newest earlier fully green head and must be exactly docs/records.md. Round 3 and the net-value test stay. TRIAGE'S FLAG (reading, unchecked): the owner's option c named "when the head before the push was fully green"; a grant covers the act it names, never a variant (rule outcomes-grant-covers-named-act). My reading is that the new form skips the same or fewer pushes: it skips only when the whole delta from a fully green head is records.md, so an intervening push that changed another file blocks the skip, which the before-head form also does when that head was not green. Where the two differ is not proven. The round 3 reviewer reads this case first: if it reads the new form as skipping anything the owner's form would not, the change goes to the owner as a question before it merges. COORDINATOR READS THE FLAG THE SAME WAY 15:16 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 15:15): the owner's literal "head before the push" has no value on the ready route (a draft push, then ready_for_review), so it could never skip there; the green-head form skips there, which is the owner's aim (stop the second full CI after the ready records push). It skips fewer where a code change sits between the green head and the records push (the delta then holds more than docs/records.md). UNPROVEN: a chain of records-only pushes, where an earlier push's run was itself a skip counted as green. Plan kept: the round 3 reviewer reads those cases first; the change goes to the owner as a question before it merges if it skips anything his form would not; the coordinator will not mark it ready before that is settled. LANE QUESTION 16:03 CST Nov 14 (lane records-page-before-ready, 16:02, from draft #3426; triage read no code): the change built under owner ruling own-830-c skips the macOS, checks-windows, pointer, shoot, mutation and sweep work, but checks-windows-guard (3 shards), checks-windows-merge (5), checks-windows-rest (2) and checks-hooks gate their steps on no flag, so they still run on a records-only push (round 1 reviewer read checks.yml lines 1761-2140; the lane did not re-read; gain unmeasured). Lane recommends accepting the partial gain until measured; it builds nothing more on #3426. TRIAGE READING: the owner's ruling says "skip every job" and "sets every job flag false"; the lane's build falls short of the named act, so gating the rest is the owner's own act, not a variant. Not posted to the owner as a new question; it goes to him only if the follow-up widens past the ruling (for example, skips a job his words do not name). The gap is reported to him in the next report. R62 CARVE 16:07 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 16:06, its own call; mine to undo): the lane's follow-up gates the Windows and hooks test steps on a new output records_only_skip, which carves a records-only exception out of R62 (ruling r62, Linux and Windows CI: each suite runs once per batch, on the batch PR; owner 15:55 CST Nov 12: "A for sure, B seems good too"; the record says the full Windows guard and merge shards move into the batch PR run and stay once per batch). The coordinator told the lane to carry it on own-830-c (every job) and to cite both in the comment above checks-windows-guard and in the PR text; the round 3 reviewer judges whether the exception can fire on any other push. NOTE as asked: R62 is carved by own-830-c for one case (a records-only push after a fully green head); the owner's R62 words are not read as a limit he lifted by any word but 830 c. TRIAGE READ of r62.json: its text holds no sentence "Windows jobs run every step on a ready pull_request"; that is the coordinator's paraphrase. The record says the full shards run once per batch on the batch PR, and the first green run of the head still carries them, so the carve skips only a repeat run of the same tree plus a docs/records.md change. The coordinator has not been told otherwise: the carve reads the same to triage. #3426 has round 1 PASS at head 261098685 (record 6884867944, unread by the coordinator and triage); the follow-up changes its head, so a fresh review follows. NARROWER BUILD 17:16 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 17:15, its own pick, undoable; relayed, triage read no code): lane records-page-before-ready (#3426) hit main's lint/test_checks_step_scope.py: 63 failures after merging main; its docstring item 2 and MUST_STAY_UNSCOPED keep 27 md-reading steps unscoped, and the records page is a .md. Whether any of the 27 reads docs/records.md is unmeasured. The pick: the lane gates only what main already scopes by `code`, plus the merge, rest and mutation-report jobs; leaves the 27 steps and the Windows guard job ungated unless traced safe; re-points the 35 exact-equality pins only for steps docs-only already skips; keeps MUST_STAY_UNSCOPED. This does LESS than the owner's "every job" (ruling own-830-c); the gain is smaller and unmeasured. The lane will list which of the 27 read docs/records.md. The 17:15 pick narrows the earlier reading: the 16:02 triage line "gating the rest is the owner's own act" now stands as a different case. The owner's word covers the Windows jobs, but the pins and MUST_STAY_UNSCOPED are a guard the owner has not been asked about. If he wants the full "every job", that relaxes a pin (a guard change) and needs his word through triage; the coordinator does not recommend asking before the list exists. No owner item posted; triage posts it if the list shows a step the narrower build cannot gate.
